rounds.fact: WebMD launched in 1996 and became so widely used for self-diagnosis that 'don't WebMD your symptoms' turned into a common joke about people convincing themselves they had rare diseases.
eBaum's World built its early traffic on hosting viral videos and flash animations, and was frequently accused of re-uploading other creators' content without credit.
Woot's entire business model was selling exactly one product per day until it sold out, a simple gimmick that built a cult following before Amazon eventually bought the company.
LimeWire became one of the most popular peer-to-peer file-sharing programs after Napster's shutdown, before being forced offline itself by a 2010 court injunction.
Addicting Games grew rapidly during the mid-2000s Flash gaming boom, hosting thousands of free browser games at a time when installing a game usually still meant buying a physical disc.
